docs.title: FontLab Pens
docs.text:
FontLab Pens brings the fontTools Pen and PointPen protocol to FontLab 9. Code written against fontTools.pens uses the same class names and calls here, and the package has no runtime dependencies. You do not need fontTools inside FontLab to draw, measure, transform or reverse outlines.

The pure-Python pens work anywhere. The native pens for FontGate (fgLayer, fgShape) and FontLab (flLayer, flShape) import the FontLab modules lazily, so import fontlab_pens succeeds outside FontLab too.

from fly.pens import BoundsPen, RecordingPen, TransformPen

rec = RecordingPen()
pen = TransformPen(rec, (2, 0, 0, 2, 10, 0))
pen.moveTo((0, 0))
pen.curveTo((0, 50), (50, 100), (100, 100))
pen.closePath()

bounds = BoundsPen(None)
rec.replay(bounds)
bounds.bounds  # (10, 0, 210, 200)

The examples import through FontLab Fly (fontlab-fly>=1.3.0), whose fly.pens alias points at this package. from fontlab_pens import RecordingPen works the same without Fly.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• The fontTools pen families: base, point, transform, recording, filter, measuring, reversing, rounding and Qt painter pens.
  • Native writers and readers that draw into, and read from, a FontLab layer or element.
  • Stroke plans that copy open contours into several layers with different widths.
  • Twelve example Scripts for FontLab's Scripts menu.

Parity tests send the same drawings to fontTools and to this package and compare the recordings, bounds and areas.

docs.title: Running the tests
docs.text:
./test.sh

This runs pytest on Python 3.11 through uv. fontTools is installed only for the tests, and coverage must stay at 80% or above. The command installs the checkout with --with-editable: pytest's pythonpath = ["src"] does not reach subprocesses, and isolated Python (-I) ignores PYTHONPATH. Without that install, seven subprocess import checks fail.

docs.title: Parity with fontTools
docs.text: tests/test_parity.py sends the same scripted drawings to the fontTools class and to the fontlab_pens class, then compares recordings, bounds and areas. The drawings cover lines, cubics, super-beziers, multi-off quadratic strings, off-curve-only (None-terminated) TrueType contours, open contours, components and transforms. The relevant upstream fontTools tests are ported in tests/ported/.

docs.title: Known FontLab behaviour
docs.text:
• A native commit can leave partial geometry if a later write or notification fails. The exception propagates and the pen stays spent; drawing again with another pen can duplicate geometry. An exception inside the drawing body commits nothing.
  • With the default notify=None, layer appends keep existing raw element payloads. Cached glyph.fgGlyph snapshots and expanded dependent component views may stay stale until FontLab rebuilds them.
  • History initialization makes the first Undo after a notified write restore the previous geometry. It does not make whole-font history safe: the notification can change timestamps of unrelated glyphs, and history is scoped to the glyph window.
  • FontLab's smooth property setter can move neighbouring handles, so FlPointPen writes the raw Smooth flag after building the contour. G2, Hobby and raw control-node flags are not represented by the point protocol's boolean smooth.
  • A closed quadratic contour that starts with an on-curve qcurve and no preceding off-curves reads back as line. The geometry is identical; FontLab stores both as "on".

docs.title: Building this site
docs.text: The site source is src_docs/mkdocs.yml and Markdown under src_docs/md. src_docs/build.sh builds it with ProperDocs and the MaterialX theme into docs/. Every push to main rebuilds and qualifies the generated output.

docs.title: FontLab targets
docs.text:
In FontLab a glyph holds layers, and each layer holds elements (shapes). The native pens and readers take a layer or an element. If you pass a glyph they raise TypeError. To pick a layer explicitly, use layer_of(glyph, master).

from fly.pens import FlPointPen, RecordingPointPen, layer_of
from fly.pens.fontlab import draw_points

layer = layer_of(glyph, "Regular")         # an flGlyph's flLayer
with FlPointPen(layer, notify="Draw") as pen:
    pen.beginPath()
    pen.addPoint((0, 0), "line")
    pen.addPoint((0, 100), "line")
    pen.addPoint((100, 100), "line")
    pen.endPath()                           # one new element on close
rec = RecordingPointPen()
draw_points(layer, rec)                     # components arrive via addComponent
Module Writers Readers fontgate FontGatePointPen, FontGatePen (fgLayer/fgShape) draw_points, draw, draw_contour_points, edit_geometry_ready fontlab FlPointPen, FlPen (flLayer/flShape) draw_points, draw

docs.title: How writing works
docs.text:
• Layer target: each pen session adds one new element. Element target: contours are appended to that element.
  • Coordinates are mapped through the inverse of the target's matrix, so reading the same target returns what you wrote.
  • Identifiers raise PenError, because FontLab stores none.
  • History is opt-in. notify="Draw" requires an attached flLayer, initializes layer and glyph history before writing, and notifies once. A bare element with notify is refused. Nonempty writes to a direct automatic layer are refused, with or without notify.
  • Components: an flLayer gets a live component element. An element target raises ComponentError. Every FontGate target raises ComponentError, because FontGate components exist at glyph level only.

docs.title: Getting a live glyph
docs.text:
fly.fl.CurrentGlyph() returns a FontGate glyph. Wrap it to edit the live FontLab glyph:

import fly.fl
glyph = fly.fl.flGlyph(fly.fl.CurrentGlyph(), fly.fl.CurrentFont())
layer = glyph.activeLayer

docs.title: FontGate results into the live font
docs.text:
flGlyph.fgGlyph is a detached copy: writing to it does not change the open font. To move a FontGate-pen result into a live layer, wrap the element:

layer.addShape(fly.fl.flShape(fg_shape))

flLayer.assignFgLayer currently raises IndexError: Unexpected SeqBase<T> length.

docs.title: Building native adapters
docs.text:
Code that resolves its own native target can build on the staging layer the native pens use.

Name Purpose StagingPointPen Validates each contour and passes it, complete, to append_contour(points). check_component(transformation) validates a component call. StagedPoint One staged point: (position, segment_type, smooth, name). staged_node_kinds(points) Native node kind per staged point: move, on, cubic or quad. FONTGATE_NODE_TYPES FontGate fgNode type for each kind. invert_transform(transform) Inverse of an affine transform; raises ValueError if singular.

FontGatePointPen(target, kind="layer") or kind="element" states the target kind instead of detecting it from the native type name, for wrappers and test doubles.

The fast path over the native fgPen is not implemented: that pen binds to a glyph's work shape, which conflicts with the layer-or-element rule.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: FontLab Pens needs Python 3.11 or later and has no runtime dependencies. It is not on PyPI; install a tagged release from GitHub.

docs.title: Into FontLab 9
docs.text:
1. Download or clone fontlab-python-pens.
  2. Open install.vfpy in FontLab 9: double-click it or drop it onto the FontLab window.
  3. Restart FontLab.

install.vfpy is a short stub that hands the work to FontLab Instamix. If Instamix is missing, the stub installs it from PyPI first. Instamix then installs the package into FontLab's own site-packages and records it under the extension id com.fontlab.pens.

The examples and Scripts also need FontLab Fly 1.3.0 or later, which provides the fly.pens and fly.fl aliases. Install Fly separately; older Fly releases without fly.pens cannot run them.

docs.title: Into a Python environment
docs.text:
uv pip install "fontlab-python-pens @ git+https://github.com/fontlabcom/fontlab-python-pens@v1.0.9"

Replace v1.0.9 with the release you want. Outside FontLab the pure-Python pens work fully; the native pens need FontLab's fontgate or fontlab module and raise when you call them without it.

docs.title: Check the install
docs.text:
import fontlab_pens
print(fontlab_pens.__version__)

In FontLab, run this in the Scripting panel. A version number means FontLab's Python can import the package.

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text: The repository's Scripts folder holds twelve examples for FontLab's Scripts menu. They import through FontLab Fly (from fly import fl, from fly.pens import ...), so install fontlab-fly>=1.3.0 alongside the package. Copy the subfolders into FontLab's Scripts folder, or install with install.vfpy and add Fly separately.

docs.title: Pen Basics
docs.text:
Short, numbered examples in the spirit of the old RoboFab pen how-tos. Each is a few lines of top-level code that works on the current glyph's active layer. Read them in order.

Script What it shows 01 Draw a Box Draw lines and a curve with FlPen. 02 Print the Outline A pen that prints every call. 03 Print the Points The same with a point pen. 04 Count Points A pen that only counts. 05 Bounds and Area The ready-made measuring pens. 06 Record and Copy Record once, replay into the other masters. 07 Shifted Copy A filter pen that moves every point. 08 Flattened Copy A pen that turns curves into lines.

Scripts 01, 07 and 08 add their edit as one undoable step; 06 adds one step per master; 02–05 only read. They have no safety checks, so open a glyph first.

docs.title: Package demos
docs.text:
Open a glyph in a Glyph window, select its active layer, then run a demo from the Scripts menu. Each prints one result line to the Output panel.

Script Folder What it does Recording Pen Demo Contours Appends a triangle. Transform Pen Demo Contours Appends a half-size copy of the visible contours, offset by (10, 20). Empty layers are refused. Outline Measurements Demo Reports Prints bounds and signed area without changing the font. Empty layers report bounds None and area 0. New Stroke Demo Contours Draws one open centerline from nothing and adds it to every master as a live stroke, thicker on each master. Stroke Plan Demo Contours Copies the open contours into every named layer with widths 20, 40, 60, … and round joins. Closed contours are skipped.

Drawing demos append elements, keep existing outlines and enroll one undoable history step for the glyph; the stroke demo updates all target layers in that step. Native errors propagate. If a native write or notification fails, inspect the layer before you rerun, because partial changes may remain. Live FontLab acceptance and Undo verification remain open.

docs.title: Testing a demo without FontLab
docs.text: Load a script with runpy.run_path(path) and call its recording_demo(layer), transform_demo(layer), measurements_demo(layer), stroke_plan_demo(glyph, layer) or new_stroke_demo(glyph) function with fake targets and native=.... The script's main() is the only part that touches the live font.

docs.title: Strokes
docs.text:
StrokePlan appends the source layer's open contours to named layers, each with its own stroke style, in one notification. StrokeStyle validates its parameters; an unsupported field raises UnsupportedStroke before anything is changed.

from fly.pens import StrokePlan, StrokeStyle, apply_plan

source = glyph.activeLayer.name
styles = {source: StrokeStyle(thickness=20)}
plan = StrokePlan(styles)
counts = apply_plan(glyph, plan, source=source)
# counts maps each target layer name to its new open-contour count

docs.title: Strokes from zero
docs.text:
new_stroke builds a detached stroked element from points and a style. Nothing needs to be copied from an existing pen. Add the element to a layer inside its history step. add_smart_corners adds FontLab smart corners (a negative radius makes an ink trap).

from fly import fl
from fly.pens import Cap, CapType, Join, StrokeStyle, add_smart_corners, new_stroke

def centerline(pen):
    pen.beginPath()
    pen.addPoint((100, 0), "move")
    pen.addPoint((100, 500), "line")
    pen.endPath()

glyph = fl.flGlyph(fl.CurrentGlyph(), fl.CurrentFont())
masters = [layer for layer in glyph.layers if layer.isMasterLayer]
for item in [*masters, glyph]:
    item.checkInitHistoryState(0)
for index, layer in enumerate(masters, start=1):
    style = StrokeStyle(thickness=20 * index, contrast=0.3, rotation=30,
                        join=Join.ROUND, cap0=Cap(CapType.ROUND), cap1=Cap(CapType.ROUND))
    layer.addShape(new_stroke(style, centerline, expand=False))
fl.flItems.notifyChangesApplied("Strokes from zero", [*masters, glyph])

Pass expand=True to outline each stroke: equal centerlines give compatible outlines in every master. In FontLab 9.1.9813 the strokes were created, expanded to compatible outlines (one 19-point contour per master) and given smart corners on a live font. The app's Undo and Redo stepped back and forward through both the creation and the expansion, pen parameters included. A saved and reopened copy kept the stroke's pen parameters and the smart-corner radii.

To round only some corners, pass nodes. The first corner makes FontLab move the outline into a smart-corner source, so add_smart_corners finds each later node again by contour and node index:

nodes = shape.contours[0].nodes()
add_smart_corners(shape, 30, nodes=[nodes[0], nodes[2]])

docs.title: What FontLab supports today
docs.text:
• The default styles work with FontLab's QPen on current builds.
  • apply_stroke writes the join as an integer, because FontLab misreads join names (fl#8630). It writes both caps explicitly and applies the native parameters before the QPen, so a refusal leaves the shape unchanged.
  • expand_stroke raises PenError when FontLab reports a failed expansion.

docs.title: Upstream limits
docs.text:
• Cap, proportion, contrast, rotation and remove-overlap controls, and full expansion, need the native penParameters / expandStroke API (fl#8626). FontLab 9.1.9813 has it; older builds accept thickness, join and miter limit only.
  • add_smart_corners needs flShape.addSmartCorners / addSmartCorner (present in 9.1.9813; fl#8628); older builds raise UnsupportedStroke.
  • Variants keep their rotation, but native persistence is unresolved.
  • Percentage rounding loses finer precision.
  • An expanded outline's saved stroke.join can disagree with the live value, so do not rely on join round-trips through VFJ (fl#8654, fl#8630).
  • restoreHistoryState on a glyph changed the history counter but not the outline in 9.1.9813; use the app's Undo.

docs.title: Using pens
docs.text:
A pen receives drawing calls. A segment pen gets moveTo, lineTo, curveTo, qCurveTo, closePath, endPath and addComponent. A point pen gets beginPath, addPoint, endPath and addComponent. Readers walk an outline and call a pen; writers, filters and measuring pens are pens themselves. Chain them to build a pipeline.

from fly.pens import RecordingPen, ReverseContourPen, RoundingPen

rec = RecordingPen()
pen = RoundingPen(ReverseContourPen(rec))
pen.moveTo((0.4, 0))
pen.lineTo((100.6, 0))
pen.lineTo((50, 99.5))
pen.closePath()
rec.value  # the triangle, reversed, with rounded coordinates

docs.title: Moving code from fontTools
docs.text:
Change the import and keep the calls:

# before
from fontTools.pens.recordingPen import RecordingPen
# after
from fontlab_pens import RecordingPen

PenError subclasses fontTools.pens.basePen.PenError when fontTools is installed, so either except clause catches it.

Not ported: DecomposedTransform, the decomposing filter pens, and the pens that need a graphics toolkit, cu2qu or a TrueType glyph object.

docs.title: Writing your own pen
docs.text:
Subclass BasePen for a segment pen or FilterPen to change calls on their way to another pen:

from fly.pens import FilterPen

class ShiftPen(FilterPen):
    def moveTo(self, pt):
        self._outPen.moveTo((pt[0] + 50, pt[1]))

    def lineTo(self, pt):
        self._outPen.lineTo((pt[0] + 50, pt[1]))

A complete version also overrides curveTo and qCurveTo; see the Shifted Copy script.
